notes: Multiple overlapping serial systems; the page advises using data-plate MFR date, ANSI standard date, condition and appearance to disambiguate overlapping styles. Page Style 1 (2002 onward) is documented as used under the Trane, American Standard, Ameristar and Ingersoll Rand names; the page also names GE among brands under which these styles appear. Known-context correction: the page documents the letter-year system from 1983 (not from 1987) through 2001, then the year-first digit system from 2002. Parent per the page header is Ingersoll Rand; the page history notes the 2020 rename to Trane Technologies. HELD, NOT SHIPPED: page Style 7 (8-character serials, documented serial F9190391 with no stated decode; year positions inferred only from similarity to page Style 3) and page Styles 4 (1981-1983, year letter in first or last position depending on product type, ambiguous letter wording), 5 (single-digit year + month letter with no table, decade ambiguous 1970s vs early 1980s), 6 (third-to-last letter year, last two digits week, 1980-1982, no L/M/N letter table), 8 (European; page states it cannot be decoded from any known chart).

styles.notes: Single-digit year encoded as a digit-keyed letterTable because the schema digits kind cannot express a 1-character year slice; the mapping (digit d = 2000+d for 2002-2009) is the page's stated rule. CAVEAT: the page notes some circa 1978-79 models may have used this shape, so a leading 8 or 9 could be 1978/1979 on a very old unit; condition and appearance disambiguate per the page. Digit-led serials starting 20-26 are genuinely ambiguous with the 2010+ two-digit reading (page notes styles overlap); style-2 claims those, so the decoder returns the 2010+ reading and the data-plate MFR date must disambiguate.

Year-prefix range 10-26 in the pattern must be extended as the calendar advances; the century rule alone would misread pre-2010 digit-led serials. Digit-led serials starting 20-26 are genuinely ambiguous with the 2002-2009 single-digit reading (the page notes styles overlap); the decoder returns the 2010+ reading, so use the data-plate MFR date to disambiguate.

Letter table: the page's chart is an image that text fetch cannot OCR. Anchors confirmed in page text: S = 1986, Z = 2001, F = 1991 (page example F23456789, 23rd week of 1991), C = 1988 (page example C01D47415, 1st week of 1988); header examples are consistent with R = 2000 and M = 1997. Remaining mappings corroborated by independent published Trane charts. DISCREPANCY FLAGGED: page text says letters A, I, L, O and Q were not used, yet the standard chart reading (corroborated by three independent sources) gives L = 1996; L = 1996 is included pending visual chart verification. The page warns this style is easily confused with page styles 3, 4, 6 and 7.

styles.era: 1970s onward, factory letter + 2-digit year + month letter, 9 characters (page Style 3)
styles.notes: Page states the 4th position encodes month but gives no letter-to-month table (the documented example's 4th character is M), so month is not encoded. The page warns this style is easily confused with page Style 2; ordering (letter-year style tried first) plus week-range validation resolves most collisions, since a page-Style-3 serial whose factory letter is in the year table and whose year digits are 01-53 would otherwise decode as a letter-year serial.
